steps.text: Autumn, 1031
The nomadic city of Kazdel, Kazdel

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Hey, l-let me through already!

steps.name: Impatient Civilian
steps.text: Hey, no shoving! You want a good spot, I'll trade you mine for some high-purity Originium out of the mines.

steps.name: Impatient Civilian
steps.text: Don't just grab the leaflet out of my hands! Eurgh, that blood all over you stinks...

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Can't help it when you're breaking into dead people's houses. Lin...go...nes... That's how you read that word, right?

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Where's Lingones?

steps.name: Impatient Civilian
steps.text: Gaul.

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Oh. Where's Gaul?

steps.name: Impatient Civilian
steps.text: How the *Sarkaz swearing* should I know where Gaul is?!

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Hey, what's with the attitude?

steps.name: Impatient Civilian
steps.text: Shh! The Highnesses and the Royal Court bigshots are discussing something in the chamber. I heard it's about reorganizing the city. Haven't you noticed all the extra guards on the streets recently?

steps.name: Impatient Civilian
steps.text: So quiet down a bit!

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: *sigh* Weather's been real stuffy today.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: It is decided.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The Military Commission will replace the War Council in assisting the King of Sarkaz Theresa in decision-making related to Kazdel's military and political affairs.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The Military Commission will be the sole administration of Kazdel, and none will have the authority to issue commands to the Sarkaz in the Royal Court's name.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: All present have already received the details of this resolution. To the Royal Court leaders who still wish to cling onto the War Council...

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Know that the Military Commission of Kazdel will become the final bastion of the Sarkaz, our eternal fortress, and the usher of a new order.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Are there any further questions?

steps.name: Banshee
steps.text: Your Highness appears more haggard than you did yesterday.

steps.name: Banshee
steps.text: Please, look after your health. No Military Commission is worth it...

steps.name: Banshee
steps.text: If it comes at the cost of Your Highness's health.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Laqeramaline... thank you.

steps.name: Laqeramaline
steps.text: I know how hard you have worked for this day... and I also know how Kazdel today views the Banshees of the Convallis.

steps.name: Laqeramaline
steps.text: But before I state our position, I encountered a lost envoy of the Liches on my journey here. He entrusted me with a letter for your Highnesses.

steps.name: Laqeramaline
steps.text: That he couldn't even find the road here... let this be proof of the immense changes Kazdel has undergone.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Hmm... A letter from Leithanien.

steps.name: Laqeramaline
steps.text: If things are going as expected, Your Highness's Messenger would still not have received any news from the Cyclopes.

steps.name: Laqeramaline
steps.text: Rather than waiting for the response from deep in the blizzard, should we not hear how the Liches of Leithanien answer?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You're right. It has been... a very long time since the Sarkaz were able to truly unite.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Oh?
The ornate calligraphy upon the letter turns into silken threads that float above the paper and weave into the shape of a familiar figure.

steps.name: Laqeramaline
steps.text: Fremont, a Lich who has long resided in Leithanien. It appears that he is now the 'First Scribe' for the Liches.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It seems that the Arts practiced by the Liches of Leithanien have seen some stylistic changes. Oh, he appears rather excited.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Why is there only image, but no sound?

steps.name: Laqeramaline
steps.text: Well...

steps.name: Laqeramaline
steps.text: The Lich envoy did suggest to me that he was rather vexed with refining his master's words, but never did I imagine that he would simply erase all the sound.

steps.name: Laqeramaline
steps.text: In short, Fremont apologizes on behalf of the Liches. They are enthralled as ever by their quest for knowledge, and are therefore unable to afford the distraction of making the long journey here.

steps.name: Laqeramaline
steps.text: But if Kazdel were ever in need of their knowledge, they would happily throw wide the gates to their temple for the people that they have chosen.

steps.name: Laqeramaline
steps.text: I am sure that with your abilities, your Highness can understand Fremont's attitude on the matter from his image alone. To me, it appears as though he is sensitive to drastic change, as has always been his wont.

steps.name: Laqeramaline
steps.text: Ah, yes. There is another letter from Fremont, one addressed directly to the General.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Might I remind you, Laqeramaline, that you are nobody's Messenger.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You have not yet expressed where the Banshee Court stands.

steps.name: Laqeramaline
steps.text: I assumed that we had reached an understanding in the course of our reminiscing yesterday. The Banshees will not participate.

steps.name: Laqeramaline
steps.text: We are still recovering from the wounds inflicted by the past war.

steps.name: Laqeramaline
steps.text: Perhaps other Sarkaz will castigate us for this, but all present should know that since that war, the elegies have yet to cease in our valley. We had suffered grievous losses.

steps.name: Laqeramaline
steps.text: If Kazdel calls on the aid of the Banshees once more, then I will give the same promise as Fremont. The Banshees will be there.

steps.name: Laqeramaline
steps.text: But until that day, you will find us willing but unable. Naturally, I myself will render what little assistance I am able to give, from this day onwards.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: That's more than we could ask for... Thank you, Laqeramaline.

steps.name: Laqeramaline
steps.text: You are welcome, Your Highness. You know where I stand. For the past hundred years, I have always stood by the decisions you have made.

steps.name: Laqeramaline
steps.text: I can only hope that your brother does not blame us for watching from the sidelines.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Next, lord Nezzsalem, the Nachzehrer King.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You were once the leader of the War Council, and the mentor of Theresis and I.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: What is your opinion on these many proposals? Where do the other council members that you represent stand on the matter?

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Have you discussed them with the Damazti Cluster?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: They have long since taken root in Kazdel, under many different names and faces. We have had many conversations over the years, and they have no objections.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Then I have no objections of my own.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Your Highness need not worry about the bureaucratic hurdles, policy imperfections, or enforcement mechanisms. Where I stand is also where the other members of the Council stand.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: We all know what we truly long for. A turnabout. A change. A banner.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Go. Do as you will.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: We will, Nachzehrer King. I promise you that.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: I trust that this stagnant and dulled 'war' can take on a new form in your hands.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I notice you have not said a word this entire meeting...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Sanguinarch of Vampires.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: To take the War Council and the century of history behind it...

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: ...And sweep it into the gutter alongside the exalted Heroic Age and what little triumphs within. Is that the General's decision?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: It is our decision.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Speak your mind, Duq'arael.
Duq'arael lowers his gaze.
Theresa's white skirt is mottled with many a blackened bloodstain.

The Sanguinarch is highly attuned to such matters. He senses the blood of the lowly, the foul stench of fallen descendants, and the murky taint of Royal Court members who willingly debased themselves.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: I thank Your Highness, for purifying the filthy blood that I so abhor in my stead.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: But never have I needed to hide my requests behind honeyed words. Such as it has been for every King of the past, and so it will be for you.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: The Military Commission is merely an attempt to hide Sarkaz witchcraft and blood behind a 'more modern, more efficient' name.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: Truth be told, I feel like this is insignificant. More than insignificant, it is simply not necessary.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You reject the proposal...?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: On behalf of the Vampire Court?
Duq'arael glances at Theresis, but Theresis remains indifferent to him.
Time has left almost no trace on the mixed-blood Sarkaz.
He stands steadfast by Theresa's side, the same nameless warrior who stood by the seamstress a century ago.
His eyes never fall on the Vampire.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: Not a rejection, no. I am merely expressing some minor frustrations about this meeting.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: You are great and powerful, all of you are. How long has it been since so many members of the Royal Court have gathered here in Kazdel?

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: Not to mention that it was you who defeated that foolish coalition in the prior age and wrestled the future into your own hands, before personally establishing the War Council.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: And now you wish to personally 'change' this Council? Why?

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: Look about you at the other dignitaries in this chamber.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: You have long reached a consensus. The only obstacle to your Military Commission is myself—and the Vampires.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: You would foist some ridiculous title upon me before forcing all Vampires to bow down to your Commission．

spans.text: You would foist some ridiculous title upon me before forcing all Vampires to bow down to your

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: When did you learn this political trickery that those Victorians and Leithanians so love?

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: Why not just take my head here and now, and slaughter the Vampires within this city's walls?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: This meeting was not convened to persecute anyone.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: Was it not?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It was convened to discuss how to bring Kazdel into a new age—

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: 'A new age'?

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: In that so-called 'Age of the Six Heroes' the songs love to praise, what I saw was bloodthirst and violence.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: I had thought that when I arrived in Kazdel, I would be greeted with the sound of Yliš's wailing, but what did I see instead?

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: I saw the coalition routed. Witchcraft, enough to cover the land and fill the skies, crushed the enemy front. The power of the Sarkaz shook the earth.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: I felt amazement. I felt... excitement. Spurred by my passion, I took the head of the Leithanian envoy who had orchestrated the coalition and offered it to the War Council.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: Nezzsalem!

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: That war was the true beginning of a new age. I thought you would agree with me.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: Have you too succumbed to schemes and politics... and shut your ears to the echoes of the abyss?

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: The abyss has no place for you, Duq'arael. Do not drag me into your tantrum.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: Ah, my apologies. But I am curious—what position did they offer the esteemed Sarkaz master of war in the Military Commission that has rendered even you so shortsighted?

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: All I await is the next war.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: And what war would that be?

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: If it pleases you, Your Highness.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Come, Duq'arael.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: I will show you.
Theresa nods her head in silent approval.
The King of Sarkaz's emotions envelop the entire chamber and all the members of the Royal Court.
Through the King's eyes, they see ruination and grief.

a.text: They see the century-old order that the Gaulish Empire so painstakingly maintained within the Core region obliterated by the combined forces of Ursus, Victoria, and Leithanien.
They see Lingones, the 'Capital of the World', doomed to never again appear on a map of Terra.

steps.text: Those present recall the campaign that reduced Kazdel to dust.
But it is not yet over.
An even further future. An even further fantasy. An even further possibility.
It is no longer a story to reflect upon. Rather, it is a speculation, a deduction, a prediction, and a verdict.
But none question it, for all possibilities must be treated equally, even for the one they see.
And its ending is equally significant and indisputable as any other.
It is a change, a turning point in history, a divergence of fate.
A crucial war looms on the horizon. It will span from now into the distant future, impacting every Sarkaz and all of Terra.
All present has seen their positions in that war.
The roles that they wish to play.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: You should understand now, Vampire. You should understand what these visions mean.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Or perhaps you have begun to grow weak and feeble as Yliš in the short span of a hundred years? You were once a warrior.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: ...I cannot deny that.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: But are you saying that a new and reborn Kazdel requires the Royal Court to relinquish its former authority?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Close, but not quite.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The new Kazdel will no longer require the Royal Court's former authority.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: It will be 'more modern, more efficient', Duq'arael.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: How can the Sarkaz speak of unity while you continue to indulge in your noble bloodlines? Will it come from the 'rule' of the Royal Court?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You may still rule over your own court, and maintain the power and prestige you hold among the Sarkaz, but the Vampire Court must yield to the Military Commission.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: I promise you this, in Theresa's name.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: When the age that you witnessed comes, Kazdel will no longer be a single dot upon the map.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: It was once more than just a city. And so it shall be more again.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: It seems I have spoken out of turn. Please, continue, Your Highness Theresa.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The aftermath of the ongoing conflict, enough to reshape current power dynamics, will engulf us all. It may come in fifty years, in ten, or perhaps even tomorrow...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Kazdel cannot escape it.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The Damazti and I both saw the visions of the campaign that will destroy Lingones.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: High-efficiency command systems made possible by Originium Arts, high-speed battleships that can break through front lines, maneuver tactics that can mobilize entire legions... new advancements are applied to the battlefield as we speak.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Their capacity for destruction is surpassing our innate instinct rooted in our bloodlines.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: What worries me more is the fact that we will still find fellow Sarkaz among the countless casualties of war.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Gaul employed Royal Court casters and the Liches in Leithanien are killing each other in battle, while a certain Wendigo is spilling the blood of his fellow Sarkaz to prove his loyalty to the Ursine Tsar.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: As for the Sarkaz mercenaries sent to the frontlines as Arts fodder, they won't even be counted in any nation's casualty statistics.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The Sarkaz massacre one another in wars we have no stake in, regarded as disposable goods to be abandoned without care by the leaders of those wars.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: For the sake of keeping pace with these changes, the Sarkaz must once again gather around the furnace. And if necessary...

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The power to dominate the war must lie in our hands.
Theresis looks to Theresa, waiting for her opinion.
But Theresa does not speak, her eyes placid, as before.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: We will plunder the other nations, and wrest their most profound secrets from them.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: We were once the proud Teekaz, forced to become the Sarkaz and derided as devils...

spans.text: We were once the proud Teekaz, forced to become the Sarkaz and derided as

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Because the outlanders feared us. It is an ancient fear, rooted deep in their hearts.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Let us remind them. Let us show all of Terra our history and legend that have been either forgotten or falsified.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The Sarkaz are not weak. We do not need others to save us from our fate.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: On the contrary, we will dictate the fate of Terra. Dictate how this land should move forward.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The details of our plan have been delivered to all present, through the runic Arts of the Banshees.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Duq'arael.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Do you still hold doubt?

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: No. Exceptional work, Theresis. Set aside a seat on the Military Commission for the Crimson Court.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: It appears that our Nachzehrer King has not yet grown addled with age. But as to whether or not he could usher in such a grand feast...

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Warriors need not die in a blaze of glory. That is a vulgarity only chased by those who seek fame.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: Oh, I nearly forgot you were still here, Laqeramaline.

steps.name: Laqeramaline
steps.text: I have made myself abundantly clear from the start, Prince Duq'arael. I need only silently observe your... enthusiastic attempt at self-expression.

steps.name: Duq'arael
steps.text: How pitiful it is to look upon such a shabby little Court. I will cherish your elegies.

steps.name: Laqeramaline
steps.text: Then this I promise you. When death comes for you, the Lord of the Banshees will sing you an elegy, delivered to you by the night wind.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Set aside your chatter for another time. It seems Their Highnesses still have matters to discuss.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: The other members of the War Council will wish to know their decisions. Duq'arael, Laqeramaline, and you Damazti disguised outside the door, with me.
The Nachzehrer King nods his head towards Theresa.
The other two members of the Royal Court do not bid the King farewell. They simply follow the Nachzehrer King out of the chamber.
After the meeting's end, Theresis stays by Theresa's side, standing silently.
He knows that she will be expecting an answer from him.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You never mentioned that you would announce the plans for war to the Royal Court.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You did not refute me either.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Would I have been able to refute anything?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You are well aware of what I think. If you wanted to argue against any of it, you would have done so a few years ago.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: For now, I have them by the reins. But it's not just them, this entire city hungers for war.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I will prevent matters from heading down the worst possible path... lest the prospects of Terra's continued existence become infinitesimally small.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You must be quick about it.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I will.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: What does Fremont's letter say?
As Theresis opens the envelope, the writing vanishes before his eyes. Yet, the message has already etched itself indelibly into his mind.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: He... has surmised what would transpire during that meeting rather accurately. He has given his opinion on some matters, alongside a reminder.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Do not place all your coming hopes in one basket.
The nomadic city of Kazdel, Kazdel

steps.name: Snappy Civilian
steps.text: You with that Babel? Pah, don't count on the Military Commission to look after you all.

steps.name: Newly-Arrived Medic
steps.text: We're here to help you.

steps.name: Snappy Civilian
steps.text: Help us? My parents died at the hands of you Leithanians.

steps.name: Snappy Civilian
steps.text: You got some nerve. What, not scared of me?

steps.name: Newly-Arrived Medic
steps.text: We knew what to expect when we came here. Just needs some getting used to.

steps.name: Newly-Arrived Medic
steps.text: Besides, our captain warned us not to agitate the locals.

steps.name: Snappy Civilian
steps.text: You looking down on me?! *Sarkaz swearing*!

steps.name: Newly-Arrived Medic
steps.text: Eh?

steps.name: Snappy Civilian
steps.text: The hell is this?! Let me go!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Welcoming wave)
Do not harm him, but do make him leave.

steps.name: Newly-Arrived Medic
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I said not to deviate from our planned route, even if it is to treat the wounded along the way.

steps.name: Newly-Arrived Medic
steps.text: Sorry, Dr. Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: No matter. You handled it well. We've reached our destination.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Welcome to Babel.
Babel Office, Kazdel

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Did you manage to retrieve all our stray colleagues?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Yes. All's well with them.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The construction of Babel's facilities is proceeding smoothly. The school that you were so looking forward to is already complete.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Yet I heard that the unbeatable Dr. Kal'tsit had not too long ago been turned down. Perhaps even kicked out?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I did not foresee such a... direct refusal.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I'm not surprised at all, to be honest. To many Sarkaz, the invitation of the King is barely worth the paper it's printed on.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: On the other hand, our 'connections' with Sargon and Rim Billiton have delivered good news. As for Columbia... Some scientists have proposed a technology exchange program.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: They have their eyes on the ancient Sarkaz witchcraft, while we have need of their latest mobile farms.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It took us a century's effort to share an equal dialogue with these powers.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The results speak for themselves. You are creating new history, Theresa.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Thank you, Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But I can tell you've had a lot on your mind recently.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The Military Commission has been formally established.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Babel's existence will spark yet another near-irreconcilable conflict in Kazdel.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Our staff comes from different races and nations. How should they live alongside the Sarkaz?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If your efforts to soothe enmity and prejudice instead become a fuse to spark conflict anew, what does Your Highness plan to do?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: If we cannot even eliminate prejudice and hatred within the walls of Kazdel, how can Babel hope to achieve equality for the Sarkaz throughout all of Terra?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: There will be members of the Military Commission posted to Babel soon. They will ensure the safety of our people.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: This will also serve as a warning to some.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Babel is backed by both Theresis and me.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Oh, right! Did I ever tell you how I met a Sankta Messenger, Kal'tsit?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Strange. The Sankta do not generally dare to approach the borders of Kazdel. Was this why Your Highness disappeared this afternoon?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Was it that obvious? I thought Laqeramaline had me covered.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The Lord of the Banshees clearly tried, but judging from the results, she isn't the best pick for clerical work.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Well, what of that Sankta Messenger?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: He was getting water from the river, and we struck up a conversation. We chatted about many things. History, peace, hatred.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Our viewpoints did not align on most things, but I could sense in him wisdom and intelligence beyond his years.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: He had thoughts concealed within his heart, ones even he did not know of.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: And so...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You used the power of the King of Sarkaz on a Sankta?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I simply wished to know what this fated encounter meant.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And... what did it mean?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It's still hard to say. But while I was looking at his soul, I felt that, perhaps... we are not so alone, Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Many on this land are doing all they can to pursue hope. Hopes big and small, hopes bright and beautiful.

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Ugh... That hurt... Are those people nuts or something? I just wanted to get a few nice things for myself, never even heard of any Babel...

spans.text: Ugh... That hurt... Are those people nuts or something? I just wanted to get a few nice things for myself, never even heard of any

steps.text: He steadies himself against the wall, gasping for air as his vision begins to blur.
Fatigue floods his limbs, weighing him down.
Through his blurred vision, he sees another in front of him fall to the crazed attackers' blades. He knows he will be next.

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: I refuse to die here...

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: It's you or me, you bastards! Out of the way!
He uses the last of his strength to barrel his way out, but the only resistance he meets is solid ground.
All he sees is black.

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: Are you alright? Were you trying to save me just now?

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: There's so much blood. Why does it feel like I'm the one saving you?

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: Hold on, I'll bring you to Babel! Our doctors there can help you!

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Hah... I'm still alive...

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: Hmph, who would have thought that those lunatics would decide to attack innocent bystanders in broad daylight to get at Babel. I don't know how the others are faring...

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: Hey, hey! Stay with me! I still don't know your name!

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: I'm... Good...luck...

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: Huh?
For the first time, he regrets giving himself this name.
